ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, two hemispherical bodies $A$ and $B$ with masses $m$ and $2m$ respectively are placed on a rough horizontal ground. A hemispherical body $C$ with mass $m$ and a smooth outer surface is placed between $A$ and $B$. All three bodies $A$, $B$, and $C$ are in a state of rest, with $A$ and $B$ just touching each other and no force acting between them. It is known that the radii of $A$, $B$, and $C$ are all $R$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between $A$, $B$ and the ground is $\mu=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}$. The maximum static friction is considered equal to the sliding friction, and the gravitational acceleration is $g$.

1. Find the magnitude of the supporting force $N$ exerted by $A$ on $C$.
2. Find the magnitude of the normal force $F$ exerted by the ground on $A$ and the magnitude of the frictional force $f$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the left and right hemispheres are labeled A and B respectively, and are placed on a rough horizontal ground; above the middle there is an inverted hemisphere C, and the curved surface of C is in contact with the curved surfaces of A and B respectively. A and B are just in contact near the middle of the ground, and the problem statement says that there is no interaction force between the two. Since the three hemispheres have the same radius, the normal at the contact point is along the line connecting the two circle centers, and the two left and right contact normals both make an angle of 60° with the horizontal. Then reason: perform a force analysis on C. C is subjected to gravity mg downward, and to the supporting forces N_A and N_B exerted on it by A and B, with directions upward along the two 60° normals respectively. C is in equilibrium in the horizontal direction, so N_A cos60° = N_B cos60°, that is, N_A = N_B = N. Equilibrium in the vertical direction: 2N sin60° = mg, therefore N = mg/(2 sin60°) = mg/sqrt(3) = (sqrt(3)/3)mg. Perform a force analysis on A. A is subjected to its own gravity mg downward, the supporting force F of the ground on A upward, and the friction force f of the ground on A horizontally; the reaction force of C on A has magnitude N, along the same normal in the opposite direction, directed down to the left, with horizontal component magnitude N cos60° and vertical component magnitude N sin60°. There is no force between A and B. From equilibrium in the horizontal direction, f = N cos60° = (sqrt(3)/3 mg)(1/2) = (sqrt(3)/6)mg. From equilibrium in the vertical direction, F = mg + N sin60° = mg + (sqrt(3)/3 mg)(sqrt(3)/2) = mg + mg/2 = 3mg/2. Verify the friction condition: μF = (sqrt(3)/6)(3mg/2) = (sqrt(3)/4)mg, which is greater than the required f = (sqrt(3)/6)mg, so rest can hold.
